title: Uniform approximation by a sparse polynomial
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for its Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and set $L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. For every $\delta>0$ and nonnegative integer $s$ satisfying $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, there is a multilinear polynomial $q(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with at most $s$ nonzero coefficients such that $|f(x)-q(x)|<\delta$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a nonzero real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, where $L$ is the sum of the absolute Fourier–Walsh coefficients of $f$
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n>0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$, $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$, and $L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$.
For every $\delta>0$ and $s\in\mathbb N$ with $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, there exists a real multilinear polynomial $q(x)=\sum_Sa_S\chi_S(x)$ satisfying
\[
 |\{S:a_S\ne0\}|\le s
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \max_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}|f(x)-q(x)|<\delta.
\]
